reason: The upsert at export-transactions.ts:281 is for transactions in categorized.toExport; the trigger at :456 is for categorized.toSyncAttachments, which categorizeTransactions (:527-578) makes disjoint from it, so the upsert does not owe this job. The related job (:329) is repaired on re-export because a synced record with missing attachment mappings falls into toSyncAttachments (:556-570).

The document_uploaded notification at process-document.ts:45 is best-effort (try/catch, 'Don't fail the entire process' at :56-63) and only reports the upload, which did happen. If the job fails before updateDocumentWithRetry (:118), BullMQ retries it and the final-failure handler (comment at :536-537) sets the status; the worst case is a duplicate activity entry.
The invoice_scheduled notification at invoice.ts:567-580 is explicitly fire-and-forget, with .catch() and the comment 'Ignore notification errors - invoice was scheduled successfully'.
createStripeProducts in lib/db/seed.ts:6-40 is a one-off developer seed script; a partial run leaves test-mode Stripe products that can be cleaned up. No production flow relies on it.

deleteAccount soft-deletes the user (actions.ts:317-323) and only then deletes the team_members row (:326-333), without a transaction. After a failure in between the user cannot log in (getUser filters deletedAt, queries.ts:29) and so cannot retry; the orphaned membership stays visible and nothing cleans it up.

groupRelatedInboxItems (inbox-upload.ts:229-239; inbox.ts:2242) is best-effort grouping in its own try/catch, and its groupedInboxId write is valid whether or not process-document is enqueued. If triggerJob throws at :241, the catch at :272-283 resets the inbox to 'pending'.

In the Stripe webhook the invoice_paid notification (stripe/index.ts:122) runs inside a try whose catch deliberately returns 200 (comment at :296-297). A crash before responding makes Stripe retry, and updateInvoice is idempotent; losing the notification is a documented tradeoff.

remind enqueues send-invoice-reminder (invoice.ts:614) and then sets reminderSentAt (:622), which is only displayed conditionally (dashboard invoice/activity.tsx:102); a missing timestamp is cosmetic. The same order is used on purpose in mcp/tools/invoices.ts:819-830.

The inbox_new notification (sync-scheduler.ts:253-273) is best-effort in try/catch. If updateInboxAccount (:283) does not happen, the next sync starts from the old lastAccessed and skips already-ingested attachments by referenceId (:137-147); the worst case is a duplicate notification.

Same best-effort document_uploaded notification as #2 (process-document.ts:44-63). If the job fails before triggerJobAndWait('classify-document') at :472, BullMQ retries and the final-failure handler sets the status.

Same pattern as #7: the invoice_refunded notification (stripe/index.ts:212) after the refund status update; errors are swallowed and 200 returned (:290-298); Stripe redelivers after a crash before the response.

initial-setup.ts:44-57 is a BullMQ job: a failed triggerJob is rethrown (:71) so the job retries; re-registering the scheduler and the scheduleId update are idempotent, and the scheduler registered at :29 runs inbox-sync every 6 hours anyway.

In signUp's invitation path the invitation is marked accepted (actions.ts:166-169) and ACCEPT_INVITATION logged (:171) before the team_members insert at :210, without a transaction. A failure in between leaves a user without a team who cannot sign up again (existingUser check at :118; the invitation is no longer 'pending', :157).

unmatchTransaction clears inbox.transactionId (inbox.ts:1490-1505) and deletes attachments (:1513) before resetting the transaction's taxRate/taxType (:1537), without a transaction. If it fails before the reset, a retry finds no transactionId (:1434), so the stale tax fields are never cleared.
seed() in lib/db/seed.ts:42-74 is a one-off developer seed script; a partial run leaves dev data reset by recreating the database.

For manual accounts, import updates balance and currency (transactions.ts:213-218), then enqueues import-transactions (:221). If the enqueue fails, the mutation errors and the user can re-run the import; the update is idempotent.

The process-document trigger at process-attachment.ts:113-134 is explicitly non-critical (try/catch, 'Don't fail the entire process', 'classification happens separately'); after a crash following updateTransaction (:93) BullMQ re-runs the idempotent job.

If enqueueing fails after the status is reset to pending (documents.ts:184-194), the document stays pending; the dashboard flags documents pending for more than 10 minutes (isStaleProcessing, dashboard utils/document.ts:18-27) and offers a retry/reprocess action (tables/vault/columns.tsx:279-286).
